corrections.why: The record's point is the 1975 museum site at Solomons. The museum gives the original 1883 site as 38 deg 19 min 03.5 sec N, 76 deg 24 min 56.5 sec W, about one-sixteenth nautical mile south of Drum Point. Decide which point the map should show; the museum's point is the original site.
The museum says the 1883 red light stood 'from a height of fifteen feet' (about 4.6 m). The record's 14.3 m looks like a different measure. Human check against the Light List before changing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two sources (the museum and the Society) give Benjamin N. Gray; LighthouseFriends's narrative says M. The story uses N and notes the variant.

The nomination form is dated 1972 and the property was nominated in April 1973 (nomination text), and LighthouseFriends gives listing in 1973. The museum's page says it was nominated in 1976; the story does not use that date.

The National Register nomination dates the lighthouse's isolation on the beach from 1965 and says the water receded gradually. LighthouseFriends says the bay only came three feet up the pilings by 1900 and that the lighthouse stood above dry land in the 1970s. The story gives both and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: (1) range 13 nm (museum) vs 11 nm (LighthouseFriends); the facts field uses 13. (2) Hansen's end: 1959 on the roster vs 1960 retirement in LighthouseFriends. (3) The 1933 gale is from LighthouseFriends alone: Chronicling America search for 1933 in D.C. papers returned no hits; a Maryland 1883 search returned two Westminster pages, not used. (4) Yeatman's 1919 rescue: the Bulletin 1919 text (p. 28) is OCR-damaged, so the story cites the 1918-1923 index; the year rests on the volume. Check the page image before printing the seaplane detail (not used in the story). (5) Lewis's name is OCR-garbled in the 1926 Bulletin ('Le,yi s'); the roster line and the 1924-1929 index entry (Lewis, James L., keeper Drum Point, rescue 167) support it. (6) The 1900 Light-House Board report's Drum Point entry has no scan-page index; cite the volume and check the page. (7) Anna Weems Ewalt (born at the lighthouse 1903, per LighthouseFriends) and James L. Weems, Sr. (keeper 1891-1918): no source connects them; the story says so. (8) Beatrice E. Goeshy (laborer 1931) and William M. Goeshy (keeper 1930-31): no source says how they were connected. (9) The 1911 characteristic change is from LighthouseFriends only. (10) Shoreline dates: the nomination says marooned from 1965; LighthouseFriends says by 1900 only three feet of water came up the pilings and the station was perched above dry land in the 1970s. Not reconciled. (11) LighthouseFriends says the Weems Steamboat Company's president signed the 1898 dark-sector petition; the story does not mention it, to avoid implying a family link. (12) Coordinates: the nomination's table gives 38 19 09 N, 76 25 17 W (OCR, at the NW corner); the museum's centre point is used in the correction. (13) Access: the museum says visitation is included with admission; no source confirms climbing, so the story does not say the tower can be climbed. Fact-check 2026-10-27: (a) The 1926 Bulletin prints the keeper's name as 'James L. Le,yi s' and the verb as 'render ed'; the story reads the name from the roster and the 1924-1929 index (Lewis, James L., keeper Drum Point, rescue, p. 17) and prints 'rendered'. Name matched by OCR, not by column position; check the 1926 page image before reprinting. (b) The 1900 Board report's Drum Point entry has no scan page in the index (footnote 5 says so); cite the page once located. (c) LighthouseFriends' 1933 gale and 1911 characteristic change are attributed to it, not presented as checked against newspapers or the Board. (d) Copyrighted sources (LighthouseFriends, museum) are paraphrased; the only quotations kept are public-domain Board, Bulletin, Commissioner and NRHP wording. (e) The 1854 appropriation is from the museum's text (August 3, 1854).
